title: The Moot votes its first winter measures
summary: The households gathered at Caol mhòr vote, in the same sitting that opens the Moot's book, to lay by grain against the coming winter and to keep watch on the north roads, having buried too many of their own the winter before to trust the season a second time unwarned.

title: The Doire ghlas dead voted into the Moot's record
summary: Walter Hale tells the gathered households what he counted on the rise above Doire ghlas and what the church porch's names afterward told him, and the Moot votes, without a voice raised against it, that the count stand as the north's own record of that winter's dead.

title: The granary founded at Caol mhòr
summary: The Moot sets a common store under lock in the harbour-house cellar, each household to give what it can spare, and names three keepers answerable for it: a harbour man trusted with a scale, a smith of Doire ghlas, and a widow of the hungry year who had buried two children in it.

title: The Moot's letter drafted for the council
summary: Walter Hale drafts, and the Moot amends and approves, four careful lines telling the council at Cathair dhearg of the households met at Caol mhòr and of a winter's dead the north had buried and counted without the south's knowledge, asking nothing beyond that the fact be noted.

title: Robert Carrick carries the Moot's letter south
summary: Peg Carrick's younger brother Robert, fifteen and never before further from Caol mhòr than Doire ghlas, a carter, carries the letter south to Cathair dhearg with it sewn into the lining of his coat, and is the better part of a fortnight on a road he does not know.

title: The Moot's letter received and filed
summary: A clerk at the harbour-house in Cathair dhearg takes the Moot's letter from Robert Carrick's hand, tells him it will be seen to, and sends him home with no answer; the disposal, once the letter reaches the council chamber, is three words in the state's own minute-book.

title: Ailean mac Iain and Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill sworn under-clerks
summary: On the twenty-third of an t-Sultain the council's newest under-clerks are sworn on the custodians' worn oath-book, Ailean mac Iain among them and, beside him, Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill, a council clerk's daughter of the capital who has wanted the office since she was old enough to know what a minute-book was for.

title: The council of twelve seated and its chairs filled
summary: Twelve chairs are filled at Cathair dhearg, drawn from the custodian families and the captains of the Severance war: among them Fearchar mac Raghnaill, whose company's roll was kept the summer before; Beathag nic Artair of the old custodian houses; Griogair mac Tormoid of the western shore; and Cailean mac Sheumais, who commanded a company at the fords of the western hills.

title: A councillor asks what a Moot is
summary: When the Moot's letter is read before the twelve, Cailean mac Sheumais asks plainly what a Moot is; no one in the chamber can answer with any certainty beyond Fearchar mac Raghnaill's memory of the word from a harbour clerk at Caol mhòr, and the letter is moved to be filed.

title: The gathering of northern households takes the name Moot
summary: In the weeks after its first sitting the gathering of the north's households comes, without a vote taken on it, to be called the Moot, a word one of its own pursers remembered from an old book of the humans' law, half in earnest and half against themselves.
